buckets.hint: Amounts in {cur}, nominal, per year; bucket balances apply before the month's spending. Net need = living expenses + housing (without amortization) + pillar 3a contributions + income tax − AHV − PK pension − earned income, from the planned values of the current year (for 3 buckets with guardrails: living expenses according to the guardrails, after floor and ceiling); one-off spending, acquisitions, purchases and special taxes do not count. Target for buckets 1 and 2 = years × net need. January refill: bucket 1 first from bucket 2, the rest from bucket 3, then bucket 2 from bucket 3; if the return criterion is not met, nothing is sold from bucket 3 and bucket 2 is not refilled. A surplus in bucket 1 or 2 goes to bucket 3. A: at the start of the withdrawal phase (first retirement), at a pension fund lump-sum withdrawal and at the restart after “all buckets empty”: wealth (the lump sum) goes to bucket 3 first, then as in January without the return criterion; the targets are reduced by the months of the year already passed, and the net need is extrapolated to 12 months from the months after the trigger. B: inflows go directly to their target and appear as the transfer “external → bucket 3” (one-off inflows, 3a, sale proceeds without a subsequent purchase, emergency sales), “external → reservation” (sale with a purchase in the following month) or “reservation → bucket 3” (surplus after the purchase); buckets 1 and 2 are not refilled. “Before” shows the balance before the inflow. C (look-ahead): if bucket 1 does not cover the month's spending and the return criterion is met, C1 applies: same procedure as the January refill, with the targets reduced by the months passed since January and the target of bucket 1 increased by the month's one-off spending, without the surplus transfer to bucket 3. If the criterion is not met, C2 applies: bucket 1 is refilled from bucket 2, then bucket 3, so that it covers the spending and afterwards still holds (min(reserve, months until January) − 1) months of need; bucket 2 is not refilled. The surplus transfer to bucket 3 only happens in the January refill. If all buckets are insufficient, a property is sold in an emergency sale; without a property, bucket 1 may become negative until wealth is positive again.

guardrails.hint: At the first person's retirement, the initial rate is applied to liquid wealth (without sale proceeds reserved for a purchase). Every January, the withdrawal is adjusted for inflation – except after a year of stock losses as long as the current rate is above the initial rate. If the current rate (withdrawal / wealth) exceeds the initial rate by the upper guardrail, the withdrawal is cut; if it is below by the lower guardrail, it is raised. Withdrawal = living expenses + housing costs − income and pensions (before taxes).

optimize.ruinFooter: is depleted (limit {maxRuin}). Median and P10: average and poor annual consumption across all paths and years from retirement. Volatility: average change in annual consumption compared with the previous year. Goal = ({round} % median + {round2} % P10) × (1 − {volWeight} × volatility); strategies that do not meet the ruin limit are grayed out. Fixed parameters (under “Strategy parameters”) stay as in the plan, including the floor and ceiling of living expenses if you do not let them vary.

wealth.cashHint: Cash is not part of the portfolio. Until retirement (pension fund payout of the first person), the app keeps as much cash as entered above, adjusted for inflation; a surplus goes to the portfolio according to the stock allocation, a shortfall is refilled from it. From retirement, the withdrawal strategy determines cash: “Standard” with the cash reserve (section “Withdrawal strategy”), all others with {fixedReserveMonths} months, or the 3-bucket strategy with its buckets.

withdrawal.endowmentHint: Withdrawal in January = (1 − weight) × previous year's withdrawal adjusted for inflation + weight × target rate × current wealth. At 100 % this equals the fixed rate; with a small weight, the withdrawal fluctuates little but follows wealth slowly.
withdrawal.fixedRateHint: Every January (and at retirement), the annual withdrawal is reset to this rate of liquid wealth. The withdrawal is living expenses + housing costs − income and pensions (before taxes): living expenses follow from it and track wealth; planned spending only applies until retirement. Wealth is thus never fully depleted – but spending fluctuates. A floor can limit this.
withdrawal.guardrailsHint: The guardrails determine living expenses, the buckets the investment. The bucket targets use the living expenses of the guardrails.
withdrawal.intro: How money is withdrawn from wealth and reallocated after retirement.
withdrawal.plannedHint: Spending stays as planned. With guardrails, it follows wealth; the buckets stay.
withdrawal.reserveHint: from retirement, months of uncovered spending (spending − income)
withdrawal.reserveIntra: Reserve in bucket 1 during the year
withdrawal.rulesHint: Rules: bucket 1 pays the ongoing spending. Every January, bucket 1 is brought to its target from bucket 2, and bucket 2 from stocks – but only if stocks reached at least the threshold in the previous year. Surpluses flow into stocks. If bucket 1 runs short in between, money is taken from bucket 2 and then from stocks. Before retirement, the cash rule from “Wealth & investment” applies.
withdrawal.sellRule: Sell from bucket 3 only if the stock return (12 months) ≥
withdrawal.splitHint: Allocation at retirement according to the preview (fixed returns). The buckets are years of uncovered spending (spending incl. housing costs − income and pensions).
withdrawal.stockShareHint: The stock allocation is under Wealth & investment. All other strategies calculate with a fixed reserve of {fixedReserveMonths} months.
withdrawal.vpwHint: Every January, the share of liquid wealth is withdrawn that, at the assumed real return, uses it up evenly by the planning age (annuity). The share rises with age; at the planning age, everything would be used up. Spending follows wealth and fluctuates accordingly. A floor limits this.

yearTable.taxHint: The taxes are in the row of the tax year they apply to: income and wealth tax are assessed in December but only paid in May of the following year (the cash balance only falls then). Lump-sum tax and property gains tax are in the year of the withdrawal or sale. The tax of the last, incomplete year is missing if the plan ends before December. The total over all years stays the same.
yearTable.taxTitle: Tax of the row's tax year (assessed in December, paid in May of the following year); lump-sum tax and property gains tax in the year of the withdrawal or sale.
yearTable.taxToggleTitle: Show or hide the columns with the year's taxes
yearTable.wealthHint: Wealth (liquid, real estate, pension assets, total) is the balance at year end. Total spending, withdrawal, total income and deviation from plan are monthly averages of the calendar year.{taxHint} Total spending = planned spending from the plan plus rent or mortgage interest and other housing costs plus contributions to pillar 3a. Withdrawal = what is taken from wealth (actual spending minus income, before taxes). Total income = income plus withdrawal. Deviation from plan = total income − total spending: at 0 everything goes as planned; with guardrails & co., a negative value shows how much the strategy cuts spending. Inflation per year = change in the price index in the calendar year (in the first year since the simulation start). Withdrawal rate = annual withdrawal / total wealth at the start of the year. The annual withdrawal is the sum of the year's monthly withdrawals (for incomplete years, the monthly average times 12); wealth at the start of the year is the value of the previous year, in the first year the balance at the simulation start; nominal values are always used. If the withdrawal is zero or negative, the cell stays empty; if wealth is zero or negative, “–” is shown. An asterisk (*) marks an incomplete year (first and last).
